title: Mirror-RoPE across positional domains
hypothesis: A small learned domain address and shared per-frequency direction can generate distinct rotary frequency schedules from one physical base, extrapolate beyond observed positions, and use less serialized state than independent domain frequencies while beating scalar RoPE scaling.
physical_object: One base RoPE frequency vector shared across four positional domains
mirror_coordinate: One learned scalar address per domain, combined with one shared learned direction over frequency bands

development.selection_metric: held-out long-position sin/cos reconstruction MSE after 800 Adam updates at LR 0.02

success_gate: In all three fresh worlds, Mirror held-out position MSE <=1.10x the independent-frequency control and <=0.10x scalar-scaled RoPE MSE, with at least 1% fewer serialized bytes than independent frequencies. This is a positional reconstruction mechanism gate, not language-model quality.
failure_gate: Both development worlds miss either the quality comparison to scalar/independent controls or the actual-byte saving against independent frequencies. Keep fresh worlds sealed after a failure.
boundaries: Teacher frequency deviations follow the shared address-direction form
No attention, language, cache, or perplexity claim
